changelog: PegaProx 1.4.1 - a security and fix release: a patched decoder and image library, IPv6 throughout, the history pages at 3000 and 10,000 guests, and an OVA image for ESXi. SECURITY: brotli 1.2.1 or newer is required, the decoder before it has an out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-111497) that a peer answering PegaProx could reach; Pillow 13.0 on Python 3.11 and newer for a heap overflow in its FlashPix decoder, while Python 3.10 keeps the last Pillow built for it; the CSRF origin check takes a bracketed IPv6 host and only one (#1155); open alerts and their mutes show a node's incidents only to callers with node.view, as the node pages do. IPV6: nodes are dialled over SSH at their plain IPv6 address, the HA group's node addresses, quorum and gateway check work on IPv6, and an IPv6 PBS gets its URL brackets, also through the port 80 redirect (#1158). FASTER: the metrics history is stored per cluster in parts, so reports, insights, right-sizing, costs, power and the node and guest charts read only what they show; at 3000 guests over 30 days the slowest page went from 16 s to 1.9 s and the largest request from 2.5 GB to 86 MB, and the database grows by about 7.5 MB a day instead of 98 MB. Existing history is converted in the background after the update, with the same results to the bit. Resolved and superseded drift events are pruned after a year. FIXED: a live migration hands the guest's conntrack state over when both nodes support it, as Proxmox's own dialog does (#1172); restore tests put a container back on the storages its backup names, and a subvolume without a size limit back on its own pool (#1168); the Hosts view of a node shows a failed read with a retry instead of an empty list (#1164); a support bundle no longer stalls on a long token in the logs; ESXi migrations keep the TPM state, use a guessed volume path only where the node has it and refuse a folder copy that would leave a disk out or copy an old state of it; a host PegaProx cannot place is not dialled at another host's address, and the agent address probe closes its socket. TRANSLATED: the ESXi migrations and events panels in all nine languages, Polish terminology and the migration phase tooltips. IMAGES: an OVA appliance for ESXi next to the qcow2 image, the qemu guest agent in the VM image (#1180), the Docker image on Docker Hub as docker.io/pegaprox/pegaprox, and signed build provenance for the release images. KNOWN ISSUES: Snapshot-Iterative ESXi migration is still experimental, automatic failover for PegaProx itself is a beta, and change plans have no approval gate. Thanks to everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚
prev_changelog: PegaProx 1.4.0 - know before you act: a migration preflight with one verdict per guest, a what-if simulator for failures and maintenance, restore tests that really restore, a timeline of every cluster, node and guest with a signed evidence bundle, and a hash-chained audit log, next to an All Guests table, a search language, automatic failover for PegaProx's own HA group as a beta and two security passes. KNOW BEFORE YOU ACT: bulk and cross-cluster migrations get a preflight with a verdict per guest (ready, warning, blocked), the reasons, ordered steps, what an abort leaves behind, a dry run and a Check step in the dialogs; a block can be overridden with an audited confirmation. The what-if simulator covers node loss, maintenance placement, N+1/N+2 headroom and storage, bridge, VLAN, VNet and PBS failures, marks every statement as known, calculated or assumed, weighs critical guests, tenants and proven restores, ranks single failures and gives one verdict; the maintenance dialog runs it before a node goes down. Restore tests run on a weekly schedule against real backups in isolated test copies (new MACs, links down or on a test bridge), check the guest agent, ports and commands, measure the RTO and report per guest, cluster and tenant, after a confirmation and within a size cap and a free space check. Recovery assurance shows the coverage of critical guests, a gap list and manual confirmations and exports signed evidence. The timeline of a cluster, node or guest puts audit, alerts, migrations, drift, tasks, backups, node states, Site Recovery, rolling updates and syslog errors in one view and exports the window as a signed evidence bundle. The audit log is hash-chained and checkpointed, and the compliance check verifies it and scores only the controls it could check. NEW: All Guests, one paged and filterable table of every guest across all clusters with a column picker and the actions each guest allows; a search language with AND, OR, NOT, groups, quotes and the prefixes name:, id:, type:, cluster: and pool:; automatic failover for PegaProx's own HA group by a majority lease with Make leader, Force leader and a witness, as a beta, every group starting in manual mode (#625); tenant quotas on every way a guest can land on a cluster; Power & Carbon per host with host profiles and unallocated power (#965), and power, costs and right-sizing worked out in the background with their age shown; file level restore from PBS backups into running guests (#1139); Site Recovery failover and failback of single guests, and a cancel that stops a run before its next guest; rolling updates that survive a restart or HA switchover and pause for quorum; a transfer network per cluster for cross-cluster traffic; change plans with four-eyes approval linked into config drift, as an optional record that runs and blocks nothing; config drift over firewall rules, HA rules, backup jobs and access with optional policy checks; event alerts for Ceph OSD latency, replication RPO, node clock drift, guest restart loops and old restore tests, more Prometheus series and two Grafana dashboards; the QDevice state of a cluster (#1137); a least-privilege role recipe for Proxmox VE; root passwords per node (#1136); an OIDC username claim for AD FS (#1149); PBS jobs per datastore with schedule, last run and next run (#804); charts with gaps instead of zeros, range picking and PegaProx's own 5-minute history; and an SMTP certificate check. SECURITY: a review of everything since 1.3.0 and a whitebox penetration test by CodeAnt AI. The task log, status and cancel requests for Proxmox VE and PBS check the task id before the call and the API sessions refuse paths with dot segments, a flaw that is also in 1.3.0 and older; template deploys check every redirect of the image URL; 100.64.0.0/10 counts as private again; ESXi servers get the address check PBS has; users confined to pools or guests no longer read node journals, Ceph logs, Ceph mirroring, cluster-wide report counts, node incidents, foreign snapshot policies or scheduled tasks; a tenant's user admin reads only their own tenant's permissions and IP lockouts are cleared by a global admin only; SSH does not trust a host key it cannot record; restores over a gone guest keep to the tenant's VMID range; the node shell takes the node address from the server only; the search no longer shows a deleted guest's notes on a new guest with its VMID; plus HA quorum values, power rates, the alert pattern guard, the WebSocket subscription, update paths, TLS key writes and mail addresses in the support bundle. BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: thirty-three, listed in the update dialog and on docs.pegaprox.com/getting-started/upgrade-1.4/. Most noticeable: 100.64.0.0/10 is refused where private addresses are refused, the OIDC sign-in included unless "Internal IdP / Private Network" is on; fresh installs verify the SMTP relay certificate; Power & Carbon figures drop; the weekly restore test really restores after a confirmation; a 401 or 403 from Proxmox VE, PBS or ESXi reaches the browser as 502 UPSTREAM_AUTH; tenant quotas can refuse operations that went through before. FIXES: syslog timestamps carry their offset (#1131), PBS dialogs above the corporate table headers (#1150), the task bar arrow (#1125), the node shell behind a reverse proxy and on the clicked node (#1143), no sign-out when an ESXi server refuses its credentials (#1142), bundled plugins and their settings in the package, the image and the scripts (#1134), OIDC accounts with a fallback name can be managed (#1141), ACME with the system CA store (#314), container restore from vzdump, scheduled tasks and rolling updates that stepped over a minute, drift repeats, XCP-ng rolling updates, PBS GC figures, and at 10k guests the what-if, the preflight, long searches, chart ranges and the history reports no longer hold up the server. KNOWN ISSUES: Snapshot-Iterative ESXi migration is still experimental, automatic failover for PegaProx itself is a beta, and change plans have no approval gate. Thanks to everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.3.0 - PegaProx itself becomes highly available: up to four instances form a group with one leader and warm standbys, next to automated Proxmox VE installations, bulk actions on guests, new alert sources, a second security pass after 1.2.0 and a fix for a silent data loss in the ESXi live clone migration. HA (#625): a second PegaProx can run as a warm standby of the first. It is paired once with a one-time code, pulls the shared configuration every 30 seconds, shows the clusters live and read only, and is promoted to leader by an admin when the leader is gone; the old leader steps aside as soon as it sees it was replaced, also when it comes back later. A group holds up to four instances: one leader that runs all automation and holds the configuration, up to two members the leader makes active to serve users (consoles, shells and SPICE open there, every change goes to the leader), and standbys that wait to take over. A standby hands a signed-in user's changes to the leader, which checks the account against its own users and names the standby in the audit log (on by default, switchable per instance). Members talk over calls signed with Ed25519 that are useless anywhere else or later, a removed member is refused everywhere and goes passive, and a sync never silently wipes what a member holds: whatever it would replace is kept as an encrypted copy an admin can download or dismiss, and a snapshot older than the member's configuration is refused. Schedules run in the group's time zone, and changing it moves the last-run stamps so nothing runs twice or is skipped. LDAP and OIDC sign-ins on a standby go by the synced account and write nothing there. All of it lives in a new High Availability tab in the settings, with a banner for every user on a standby, in all three layouts and all nine languages. Groundwork for automatic failover is included but not yet enabled. NODE RECOVERY: PegaProx's own node recovery moves a guest only when every volume it starts with is on shared storage, and reads a dead node's guest configs from the cluster file system on other nodes instead of guessing; a node that returns during its recovery keeps what is left and no guest runs twice; a recovery that could not finish is listed in the cluster's HA settings, where the guests whose config already moved can be started. A new self-fence agent (its own unit, pegaprox-fence-agent) decides by quorum first and asks PegaProx only where quorum cannot decide; an agent of the old kind stays as it is until it is installed again, and the HA settings show which one runs on each node. Two-node and forced-quorum clusters set up from now on are recovered only after a fence per node that was read back; existing setups keep their behaviour behind an explicit "unsafe two-node recovery" switch. NEW: automated Proxmox VE installations - PegaProx serves the answer file to the Proxmox installer, each profile with its own fetch token and every run tracked from the first fetch to the installer's post-installation webhook, with a six-step guided setup that hashes the root password on the server, an answer file editor that refuses what the installer would refuse, encrypted storage and a page of its own in all three layouts (autoinstall.view and autoinstall.manage, for accounts that see every cluster). Bulk actions on selected guests - start, shut down, stop, reboot, snapshot and tags - in every layout, each guest checked on its own and the result shown per guest; a node can start, stop or migrate all its guests at once. Favorites are stored again and show as a group at the top of the sidebar in Modern and Corporate. New alert sources: failed Proxmox tasks such as a failed vzdump, Ceph health, failing or lagging replication, a ZFS pool that is not ONLINE or shows errors, and snapshots older than a set age, each raised once with a resolved notice and mutable per rule or per object; rolling updates can alert when a run starts and finishes and when a node's reboot is handed over (#716). Bulk migration runs on the server one guest at a time, a few at once or all at once, follows each guest and can be cancelled, also across page reloads (#952). Guests that no backup job covers are listed in the All Clusters overview and can raise an alert, with a grace period for new guests and a no-backup tag for intentional gaps. Cloud can be picked as the layout at the first login. Containers can be created from OCI images on PVE 9.1 and newer, from a small catalog or any image reference (a technology preview, as in Proxmox). Rolling updates can move a node's templates with its guests (#763) and let negative affinity rules give way for the run, switched back on afterwards (#954), in scheduled runs and in a node's maintenance as well. ProxLB pin tags (plb_pin_) rank a drain's targets instead of blocking it, with switches for strict pins and an automatic move back in the cluster settings, which also list the guests off their pin and can move them back (#811). Directory mappings and virtiofs shares can be set up in the VM hardware settings, checked before they reach PVE, with a warning before a guest that uses one is migrated. The All Clusters overview lists the storage of every cluster and exports the guest inventory with vCPU, memory, disks, IPs, HA state, tags and pool. Node temperatures work without lm-sensors, read from the kernel's hwmon. A node's ZFS pools show their device tree with error counts and the last scrub. The VM hardware settings can add a VirtIO RNG, checked against what QEMU accepts before it reaches PVE. A Site Recovery test failover keeps a boot screenshot of every guest it started as evidence. The command palette finds guests by MAC address, IP and notes. Admins can show a broadcast banner to everyone or to chosen tenants and roles. Check connection runs read-only probes against a cluster (API and fallback hosts, TLS fingerprint, the token's privileges against what PegaProx needs, versions, clock, quorum, SSH) and names a fix for each failed item. Container features (nesting, keyctl, fuse, mknod, NFS/CIFS) can be changed after creation, and PCI and USB passthrough can use the cluster's resource mappings, which also work on API-token clusters. A metrics.view permission lets a Prometheus scrape run without an admin token (#818), and the exporter also reports storage use per storage, replication state and age per job, the age of each guest's newest backup and guest disk I/O. The HTTP API is described in OpenAPI, generated from the routes and naming the permission each one demands (#104, #693), and can be browsed inside PegaProx from the user menu. Also: a System theme that follows the OS (#743), plugins limited to chosen clusters (#642), PEGAPROX_CONFIG_DIR and PEGAPROX_LOG_DIR (#826), the QEMU description in the Corporate summary (#813), a per-cluster switch that turns SSH off entirely (#941), PBS servers that connect with an API token (#805), a Tools section in the Corporate sidebar, the ESXi infrastructure view in all nine languages, a refreshed cloud image catalog (Ubuntu 26.04, Debian 13, AlmaLinux and Rocky Linux 10, Fedora 44, Alpine 3.24) that passes the CPU model the EL images need, a release Docker image for 32-bit ARM, release images on Python 3.12.15, and snapshot .deb builds of the Testing branch (#973, #974). PERFORMANCE: answers on kept-alive connections no longer wait for a delayed ACK, about 2-3 ms instead of 45 ms per request; the cluster health check reads all storage in one call (#946). CONSOLE: the console behind a reverse proxy is fixed end to end - the API port is no longer replaced by the VNC port, the configured port is used where 8006 was hard-coded, the upgrade carries credentials that match the ticket, a websocket is no longer upgraded twice, a session no longer ends a tenth of a second after it opens and partial sends are completed (#945, #955, #956); clusters with only an API token open consoles (#955); an error left behind by another TLS connection no longer ends a healthy console (#713); Stable Mode keeps the frame order instead of closing with 4099 (#955); paste types the right characters on de, es, fr, it, pt, pl and en-gb keymaps (#959); the terminal follows the bind address (#957) and no longer writes its script to /tmp under a predictable name (#958); the node shell no longer lets Firefox pan the page sideways (#727). UPDATES: Check for updates refreshes apt on the nodes first, and a refresh that failed is reported as a failed check instead of stale packages shown as current; rolling updates reboot once instead of waiting out a reboot that already happened (#953), evacuate guests only to nodes they may run on under HA affinity rules and storage availability (#647), and read the debsecan urgency correctly (#827); the PBS update panel shows its lines again instead of [object Object] (#964, #971). SECURITY: a second pass after 1.2.0, over the remaining penetration test findings and the daily code scans, including defects in 1.2.0's own fixes. A delegate with admin.users could demote an administrator and replace their password in one request; read routes next to gated write routes handed out every tenant's custom roles, pool permissions, VM ACLs and the cluster security audit; an API token with a lower role than its account got its privileges back through VM ACLs, list routes and the cluster gate; a deleted VM's ACL went to the next guest on that VMID; the ESXi credential guard could be passed by leaving the password out or by disabling the server first; an iSCSI CHAP secret sat in the node's process table; replacing a second factor needed no password; storage.create was never enforced; the 1.2.0 syslog gate never worked on a locked database, validators accepted a trailing newline, and a rate-limit cap could reset the login limits; an ntfy topic URL reached the log in full and per-cluster log files still took forged lines; a logo URL could put script on the public status page; host key pins could be lost under concurrent writes; and caller-supplied list limits are bounded. The release images verify the packages they install as root. A third round, on the rest of the penetration test and the code scans of 5 and 6 October: the PVE console ticket goes only to PegaProx's own console server; an API token secret is never offered as an SSH password; a cluster edit can no longer send its stored credential to a new address or inject an SSH option; a tenant override bounds the admin it lowers; accounts limited to pools or guests make no root@pam change, write no shared storage content and place no guest; migration paths no longer pass credentials where others can read them, keep node files private and destroy only what they copied; guest routes ask the right permission and act as the right principal; installation-wide reads, the updater, drift baselines and schedules ask who may; host key pins survive unreadable files and races; slow or greedy clients no longer hold the request pool or the syslog queue; and the CI actions and images are pinned, static downloads verified and PyJWT kept at 2.15.1 or newer (#972). BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: thirty-eight, listed in the update dialog. Several take something away from an existing setup: adding storage needs storage.create, a deleted custom role grants nothing instead of the viewer set, a user whose directory group holds a pool grant is now confined to that pool, node recovery leaves a guest with a local volume where it is (a local ISO included), and the cloud image ids fedora-40, debian-11 and alpine-319 are gone. Please read them before updating a multi-tenant install or one that uses PegaProx node recovery. FIXES: the ESXi live clone migration (Live Clone and Auto) lost every write made on the source after its snapshot, during the copy and during the confirmation hold (#1124); the switchover now stops the source, folds the snapshot back, compares every block and copies what changed, runs the post-copy steps only then and powers the source back on if anything fails before the target runs, so it takes longer than the few seconds it used to; the block delta of the pre-sync migration copied only the head of each changed block and still reported success, changed blocks now arrive whole and are read back; Windows guests on VirtIO SCSI no longer fail with INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE after driver injection, vioscsi gets its own bus type and the device ids it really has and the drivers go into the control set Windows boots from (#823); an Entra sign-in no longer fails with HTTP 500 when a group has no display name (#962); config drift no longer reports an offline node's objects as removed and names the outage once (#968), and a read that failed is no longer taken as a removal; reports load a whole week for Last Week, keep the newest snapshot of a window and size the storage column by the longest node name (#963), with report times in browser time; container migration with a target storage (#808); V2P disks on block storage are allocated as raw on Proxmox 9 (#816); the SMBIOS auto-configurator no longer rewrites a running VM on every cycle (#943) or fills the journal (#969); snapshot times read the same on every page, in browser time and the user's 12h/24h setting (#939); rolling updates on XCP-ng no longer stop at the first node (a 1.2.0 regression); the container dialog lists container templates again, and XCP-ng's from-template path its templates (a 1.2.0 regression); pool grants on LDAP and OIDC groups reach the user, also when typed as a bare group name (#940); a slow answer no longer overwrites the detail view of the next object opened (#828); the client portal's SSO button, the close buttons of three dialogs and Back to Login on the 2FA screen work (#810); the restart button, an update and a rollback restart PegaProx in place instead of stopping it under the Debian package's unit; Unlock all for IPs and users actually unlocks, and the security panel and the support bundle count active sessions; an ESXi host registered for migrations no longer breaks the cluster list; XCP-ng keeps one session per pool; the Cloud skin can be set as the default theme; and a node's management address is found without knocking on the SSH port of a cluster with SSH switched off. KNOWN ISSUE: the experimental Snapshot-Iterative ESXi migration mode can report success with missing or wrong data on the target; use Live Clone or Live Mirror for guests whose data matters. Thanks to everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.2.0 - a security release built on a full AI-assisted penetration test of the whole codebase, plus the tenant work that was queued behind it. SECURITY: 558 findings were triaged, every critical and high one verified against the code by hand before anything was changed, and the ones that were real were fixed with a regression test and a counter-proof apiece. One class accounted for most of them: a store that fails to load answers with an empty result, and empty was being read as the permissive answer - a tenant table that could not be read handed out every cluster, an unreadable ACL store stopped confining anybody, an unreadable schedule table let a write begin with a DELETE, and a failed settings read bound the syslog receiver's unauthenticated port on an instance that had switched it off. Those now refuse rather than guess. Log injection is neutralised at the sink instead of at seventy-five call sites, so a name carrying escape sequences can no longer repaint an operator's terminal; URLs written into logs have their credentials stripped, which matters because for a webhook the URL is the credential. SDN object ids are validated before they are used as a path segment, where '..' reached a neighbouring API object. The OIDC discovery address is pinned to the address it resolved to, and a group mapping that matches only on display name now says so. LDAP warns when neither TLS nor STARTTLS is configured - the warning used to sit inside the TLS branch, so the one setup that needed it was the one that stayed quiet. Lists that arrive in a request body are bounded, rate limiters can no longer be grown without bound by the thing they limit, and a managed node can no longer hand us output until we run out of memory. The second-factor probe fails closed on both the login and the re-authentication path, so a database hiccup no longer waves a key-only account through. BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: sixteen of them, several of which take something away from an existing setup - a node reboot now requires the node.reboot permission that was defined but never enforced, alert channels need admin.settings to change, PBS resource-wide operations require every linked cluster, ESXi delete and rename moved from vmware.vm.power to vmware.vm.manage, and a pool grant no longer opens an ESXi server. Please read the release notes before updating a multi-tenant install. TENANTS: a per-tenant disk ceiling, a per-tenant VMID slice that restore and template deployment both respect, the tenant list behind them, and self-service container creation serialised per tenant so two requests can no longer clear the same quota check. CI: the APT repository workflow can no longer be dispatched from an arbitrary branch to reach the signing key, the release version is validated before it reaches a shell, and build jobs no longer carry a token that can write to the repository. FIXES: ESXi to Proxmox migration never got past VMID allocation and had not worked since 0.9.2; drift events never reached the configured webhook channels (#815); a failed schedule read could rewrite the whole table; SQLCipher connections raised exceptions two handlers were not catching (#822); the V2P path asked a Proxmox node for a package it does not have (#824); the CVE scan names what failed and measures against the right suite (#825, #827); the console reconnect rides out more than six seconds and mints its ticket on a node that is actually up; a pool grant makes the pool's VMs visible (#793); clusters are labelled by display name everywhere (#787); last_login is recorded for OIDC and Entra logins (#794); node maintenance survives a restart when PVE HA accepted it (#720); the full Proxmox boot-order format is parsed instead of the legacy letters alone (#755); a balancing exclusion is no longer dropped when a cluster enumerates empty; a failed test failover leaves the clone stopped instead of starting it with live NICs; and the status page no longer hands database errors to the browser. Thanks to @karolina-glowinska, @Frisch12, @hugobugomugo, @si458, @mdobprv-lab, @jostrasser, @avsdev-cw, @surreal70 and everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.1.1 — a security and reliability release; every user of 1.1.0 should update. SECURITY: a full audit and pentest pass over the authorization layer closed the recurring class where reaching a cluster was treated as reaching everything on it — per-VM gates now sit on the console, termproxy, PBS, node task-log, search, tag and report paths, and pool- and ACL-scoped accounts stay inside their scope on every one of them. Live streams re-check the account behind them on their own clock and a single account can no longer hold unbounded SSE streams open. Several separately reported issues are fixed and will be described in their own advisories. Encryption-key rotation was rebuilt after it was found to commit re-encrypted rows before the new key reached disk, to miss the PBS, ESXi and VAPID secrets and clusters.ha_settings, and to leave the audit trail reading as tampered. STABILITY: a clean systemd stop that also takes the console subprocess with it (#780, #784); request-pool slots are reclaimed from idle keep-alive connections instead of starving the server (#777); an idle tab dropped from about four REST calls a second to well under one (#782); a same-named cluster no longer steals another's log handler (#783). CONSOLE: pointer latency cut by roughly an order of magnitude at a realistic event rate, the connection-pool churn behind the intermittent drops removed, and the estate-wide IP sweep given its own share of the budget so opening a console does not queue behind it (#713). FEATURES: a VM console can be opened in its own browser window and several watched side by side (#767). The interface now carries its copyright, license and source references on every screen, with the full notice under Settings > About. FIXES: node shell over IPv6 (#778); deleting a cluster purges every table keyed by it (#779); pool assignment gated on pool.assign rather than admin.users (#766); three XCP-ng and ESXi endpoints that raised instead of answering (#781); container create and destroy in the client portal (#765); cluster settings surviving a reconfigure (#762); Corporate ESXi table headers (#753); the compliance dashboard now says why a node check could not run instead of showing 'err 502' (#717); cross-cluster migration fingerprint case (#733); V2P disk copy reporting success after a failure, and an ESXi password left world-readable. Thanks to @Frisch12, @zobsg, @Panxatony, @mikelawson68, @daglimmer, @cybrwerk, @grobe0ba, @hugobugomugo, @mdobprv-lab, @si458 and everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.1.0 — a security-hardening + reliability release. SECURITY: a full Aikido AI-pentest re-triage closed 15 confirmed BOLA / IDOR / token-scope findings — a tenant-custom-role API token now keeps its role name so its cluster scope resolves correctly (it can no longer fall back to 'all clusters'); the auto-balance worker, cluster VM inventory and PBS auto-attach can no longer be reached through a pool / ACL fallback on a cluster the tenant doesn't own; and the live 'resources' SSE stream is scoped to each client's per-VM ACLs (#736). ROLLING UPDATES: evacuation no longer false-fails on 'VM is locked (migrate)' when a guest is already migrating (#647); a benign Ceph HEALTH_WARN (slow BlueStore ops) no longer burns the full 120 s wait (#747); a node that doesn't need a reboot is no longer announced as rebooting, and soft maintenance now survives a PegaProx restart (#715, #720). MIGRATION: ESXi→Proxmox with non-krbd Ceph RBD targets maps librbd URIs to a block device and routes the EFI fallback through them (#722); local snapshot-replicas preserve the source MAC / hostname (#646). CONSOLE: the PVE VNC leg serialises SSL access to stop intermittent disconnects (#713) and the noVNC proxy works under gevent on Python ≥ 3.13 (#740). FEATURES: a usable phone layout with an off-canvas sidebar drawer (#189); re-pin SSH host keys after a node's key changes, e.g. post-CIS-hardening (#717); an optional node FQDN suffix for 'Open in Proxmox' links (#689); reversible umask-027 + lockout warnings on the sshd-hardening controls (#16745). FIXES: WebAuthn / passkey-only accounts can log in (#746); PBS 'passed' disks no longer show red and the overview stopped-VM count uses the explicit stopped status (#751, #749); Corporate light / dark theme handling (#742); iLO 4 stale SEL assertions no longer latch a node Critical (#714); ACME honours the private-CA opt-in and writes issued certs where the TLS listener serves them (#730, #725). LANGUAGES: a new Polish translation (#737) and a backfill of every language to full English parity (de / zh / fr / es / pt / ko / it). QUALITY: 662 automated tests run on every PR, and contributions now carry a PR template + AI-review bar. Thanks to @mikelawson68, @cklabautermann, @Frisch12, @mluenzer, @robertdahlem, @hugobugomugo, @mdobprv-lab and everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.0.2 — a security + maintenance release. SECURITY: closes a per-VM / console access-control bypass where a Client-Portal user scoped to specific VMs could reach any VM on a tenant-owned cluster (assigned a CVE; reported by Jörg Morasch / SYMPLASSON); a broad follow-up audit closed the same object-level authorization gap across bulk + cross-cluster migrate, PBS restore / protect / notes / prune, migration history and the HA plugin, and closed tenant-delegate privilege-escalation paths (a delegate can no longer grant permissions it doesn't hold, reset a higher-privileged peer's password / 2FA, or keep console access after being disabled); and a DNS-rebinding SSRF-guard bypass is closed by pinning the validated IP for outbound requests (GHSA-hmcf-9q7f-vx35; reported by senti-man). AUTH: OIDC login no longer races itself to a logout mid-callback in Firefox (#681), and OIDC group-to-role mappings apply custom roles (#682). FIXES: adding a Proxmox cluster whose account has 2FA now shows a clear, localized message — add with an API token or temporarily disable 2FA — instead of a silent connected-then-offline (#683); the PBS disk table shows SMART health for HDDs without a wearout value (#690); the snapshot overview gained multi-select + bulk delete (#696); EFI and TPM disks accept a raw / qcow2 format (#678); the VM/CT config modal no longer reload-loops (#698) and the backup-verification modal no longer overlaps the PBS UI (#701). FEATURES: rolling updates reboot a node only when needrestart reports a required restart (#694, PR by @gyptazy); an internal / private ACME CA is supported opt-in (#685); a first-class Cloudflare DNS-01 provider was added (#687, thanks @brngates98); hardware-health rollups use live sensor / SEL state and name the contributor (#686); the prebuilt VM / LXC appliances ship sshpass so password-auth SSH works out of the box (#688); and self-update is install-method aware (apt / docker / source). QUALITY: 555 automated tests (authz, integration, SSRF, SSL-bootstrap, hardware, i18n) run on every PR; the whole branch was re-audited and E2E-verified before release. Thanks to Jörg Morasch (SYMPLASSON), senti-man, @gyptazy, @brngates98, @ranydb and everyone who filed, fixed and sponsored.

PegaProx 1.0.1 — a maintenance + feature release on top of 1.0. LANGUAGES: the web UI is now available in Simplified Chinese (#670, thanks @ranydb). CONSOLE: SPICE is offered in every VM console entry point — a downloadable virt-viewer .vv for audio / USB / multi-monitor sessions, alongside the built-in noVNC. SECURITY: another Aikido penetration-test pass closed a set of authorization / IDOR gaps — power- and cost-rate reads are now scoped to the caller's clusters (a scoped API token can no longer enumerate every cluster's rates), the client portal's reboot action is gated on vm.restart instead of vm.start, and further authz / validation / SSRF invariants from batches 1–2 are enforced; the CIS SSH-hardening control no longer disables TCP forwarding (which the built-in VNC console tunnels through), and applied hardening controls are now selectable for rollback. FIXES: adding a disk to a container now targets a container mountpoint (mpN) instead of a QEMU disk key, and never overwrites an occupied slot; a locked VM/CT can be unlocked even on token-authenticated clusters (falls back to qm / pct unlock over SSH); OIDC keeps the full preferred_username instead of truncating at '@' (#486); the storage / snapshot / backup / update action bars follow their backend permissions (#644); scheduled rolling and maintenance updates evacuate local disks by default (#630/#629); node-temperature parsing falls back to plain 'sensors' text when JSON is unavailable (#601); in-band BMC reads fall back key → agent → password so password-only nodes still report hardware health (#609); ESXi / cross-hypervisor migration lists route to their own handlers (#654). PLATFORM: ARM64 / aarch64 build artifacts are now published (#674, gyptazy); cryptography is pinned to 50 and pyOpenSSL to 26.4 to keep the vulnerable 49 line out (#650). QUALITY: 438 automated tests (authorization, integration, SSL-bootstrap, hardware, i18n) run on every PR, and the whole branch was re-audited before release. Thank you to everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.0 — out of Beta. Everything from the 0.9.x line, hardened and rounded out. SECURITY: a full post-release penetration test closed a BMC-credential exfiltration on the test-BMC endpoint, an ESXi/XCP password ever appearing on a process argv (now fed over stdin/SSHPASS), a BMC/Redfish SSRF oracle, and an SSH-amplification path in the Ceph mirror views; the TLS bootstrap now FAILS CLOSED — if TLS is the intended posture and a usable certificate cannot be loaded or generated, PegaProx refuses to start with an actionable error instead of silently serving plaintext on the TLS port (#633, thanks @SpyrosPsarras). FEATURES: cross-cluster EVPN vNets spanning multiple clusters in the same AS — create / edit / membership / drift-detection + optional reconcile and drift→alert fan-out (#612 cybrwerk); V2P/ESXi migrations gain an opt-in 'wait for confirmation before cutover' gate (#562 ajoergensen); the Top Resources table is now sortable by any column (#621 ccesario); scheduled rolling updates carry a per-schedule reboot/online timeout instead of a fixed 10 minutes (#630). FIXES: nested / hierarchical resource pools now show their members and VM counts (#634 prasannak81); ESXi→PVE migrations of multi-disk VMs to classic LVM no longer abort when a target volume already exists (#636 shepart); XCP-ng→PVE transfers resume by HTTP range instead of failing on a broken pipe (#546). QUALITY: the SSL-bootstrap, authorization and integration test suites continue to run on every PR. Thank you to everyone who filed, fixed and sponsored along the way. 💚

breaking_changes: The metrics history is stored per cluster in parts from 1.4.1 on. History written by an older version is converted in the background after the first start, newest first and at about a third of a core, so on a large install it can take a while; the pages answer the same throughout. A downgrade to 1.4.0 or older shows only the history written after the downgrade. Nothing is deleted, and the next update reads and converts all of it again (docs/history-retention.md).

Resolved and superseded drift events are deleted after 365 days (PEGAPROX_DRIFT_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS) and beyond 200,000 per cluster (PEGAPROX_DRIFT_EVENT_CAP). Open and acknowledged events and those linked to an incident or a change are always kept.
Python 3.10 installs keep Pillow 12.3.0, the last release built for it. Pillow 13.0, which closes a heap overflow in its FlashPix decoder, needs Python 3.11 or newer.

Coming from 1.3.x: the behaviour changes of 1.4.0 apply as well, first among them that carrier-grade NAT and tailnet addresses (100.64.0.0/10) are refused again wherever private addresses are refused. They are listed at docs.pegaprox.com/getting-started/upgrade-1.4/.
Coming from 1.2.x or older: the behaviour changes of 1.3.0 apply as well. They are listed at docs.pegaprox.com/getting-started/upgrade-1.3/.
